title: The Islanders
author: Yevgeny Zamyatin
publication_note: written in 1917 in Newcastle upon Tyne, first published in 1918 in Petrograd; Zamyatin died in 1937, so the text is in the public domain
source_note: Text from ru.wikisource.org, after E. I. Zamyatin, Selected Works in two volumes, vol. 1 (Moscow, 1990).

names.VI: The Face of a Cultured Man

art_alt.1_library: A vicar's library with timetables pinned in rows on the wall and the vicar standing stiffly beside a desk with a clock
art_alt.1_street: A street of identical brick houses: a red motor car has stopped, a man lies in the road with his boots in the air, a red-haired man waves four arms and a vicar looks on
art_alt.1_spare_bed: A spare bedroom: an injured man in bed with his boots under the blanket, a lady with a pince-nez, a doctor and a stern vicar
art_alt.1_night_beds: A bedroom at night under a bright moon: a vicar lies awake in a nightcap with his hands crossed, and the other bed is empty
art_alt.2_pince_nez: A lady's pince-nez lying alone on a table while she stands at a window with swelling clouds
art_alt.2_bedside: A patient in bed in the dusk and a lady sitting close beside him
art_alt.2_okelly_doctor: A timid doctor dropping his bag as a red-haired lawyer with four arms bursts into the sickroom
art_alt.3_doorsteps: A row of identical houses with whitened doorsteps and a line of identical Sunday gentlemen in top hats
art_alt.3_window_clouds: A lady at a window watching bright clouds race by, a book forgotten beside her
art_alt.3_drawing_room: A parlour full of guests in pink and blue as a tall old lady in grey enters on her son's arm
art_alt.3_okelly_enters: A red-haired lawyer in a rumpled jacket arrives late at the party while the guests nudge one another
art_alt.4_didi_waiting: A waiting room: a girl with cropped hair smoking on a sofa, a huge man at the papers and a red-haired lawyer
art_alt.6_milly: An old lady in grey carries off a white cat in indignation while a lawyer roars with laughter
art_alt.10_okelly_visit: A firelit room with a pug on the mantel: a lawyer teasing a stiff man who is counting his savings
art_alt.3_supper: A supper table: a man in a kilt, a red-haired lawyer waving an inflatable suitcase, a vicar checking his watch
art_alt.3_candle_door: A corridor at night: a lady with a candle says good night to a square-chinned man at his bedroom door
art_alt.4_office: A lawyer's office with four typists and a red-haired lawyer introducing his wives to a bewildered newcomer
art_alt.4_theatre: A music-hall: a shadow dancer on a lit screen, two men in the stalls and a lady with a pince-nez in a box
art_alt.5_pug: A cosy room with a firelit mantelpiece and a porcelain pug, a stiff man sitting on the carpet with papers
art_alt.5_church_lane: Children in white collars march by the church, followed by a vicar, a lady and a man in a kilt; a young woman leans on a railing
art_alt.5_pug_floor: A dying fire, a young woman lying on the carpet beside a porcelain pug and a man frowning in the doorway
art_alt.6_blue_vase: A dining room with the blinds down, a portrait of a square-chinned gentleman, a brass gong and a blue vase of carnations
art_alt.6_dinner: A solemn dinner: an old lady with long thin lips, a red-haired guest in a morning coat and a trembling servant in white gloves
art_alt.6_fire_letter: A girl drying her hair by the fire over scattered letters, a lawyer on a pouffe and a huge man standing silently
art_alt.7_taxi: A taxi racing at night with three people in it, streaks of lamplight behind
art_alt.7_boxing: A boxing ring under bright lamps, a blue boxer and a black boxer, a roaring crowd
art_alt.7_campbell_ring: A huge bare-chested man stands firm in the ring against the champion while the crowd roars
art_alt.7_night_room: A moonlit room: a battered man on a couch, a girl in black pyjamas by him, a porcelain pug grinning on the mantelpiece
art_alt.8_newspaper: A newspaper headline about an aristocrat boxer, with a lady and a vicar reading
art_alt.8_meeting: A parish committee: a vicar before a list of seventeen items, a man in a kilt and ladies in pink and blue
art_alt.9_pug_kiss: A girl in pyjamas holds a porcelain pug up to a shocked vicar's face
art_alt.9_bull: A big man lowers his head like a bull and walks at a startled vicar
art_alt.10_moon: A summer night in a park: a moon wearing a monocle and two shadowy figures in the bushes
art_alt.10_picnic: A picnic of oysters and champagne on the carpet, a lawyer with waving arms, a laughing girl, a woman in a pink chemise at the door
art_alt.10_iron: A dream of a gigantic electric iron gliding over a flat world, with a small man admiring it
art_alt.11_army: Salvation Army soldiers march through a bright street with banners and a drum while a woman officer hammers at a door
art_alt.11_armchair: A vicar dozing politely in an armchair as small reflected suns dance on the walls
art_alt.11_beach: A seaside beach with bathers in orange, pink and violet caps, and two figures on the sand
art_alt.11_cafe: A seaside café: a lady and a man in a kilt at one table, a red-haired lawyer with a strange parcel and a girl at another
art_alt.12_letter: An anonymous letter and a narrow blue envelope on a table, a man at a foggy window with drops running down it
art_alt.12_shop: A shop counter with thin silk underclothes, a huge embarrassed man with a box and a girl who hides her face
art_alt.12_birthday: A birthday evening: champagne, a lawyer holding out a cheque, a girl tearing paper, an iron on the mantel beside a pug
art_alt.13_lilies: A foggy lamplit street: a lawyer with white Easter lilies and a vicar with a flat hat watching from the other side

art_alt.13_dining: A bright dining room: an old lady, a vicar making a speech, a trembling lady and a seated man

art_alt.14_walk: A policeman and a huge man walking side by side down a lane between tall smooth walls in the fog
art_alt.15_prison: A night crowd outside a prison wall under a lantern, a huge grey bird above, a placard against the sirs
art_alt.15_bedroom: A bedroom at night: a vicar asleep in his nightcap and his wife sitting up beside him, screaming
art_alt.16_sun: A bright morning outside the prison: a crowd holding watches, a vicar and his wife, a little old man at the gate
art_alt.16_bell: A great brass bell and dripping drops of brass, kneeling townsfolk, a woman crying out and a vicar beside her

episodes.title: The Foreign Body
episodes.blurb: A square-chinned gentleman is knocked down outside the house of the Reverend Dooley, author of the Covenant of Compulsory Salvation, and his orderly household begins to come off its rails. Then a lawyer with four arms, four typists who are all his wives, and a porcelain pug named Johnny.

episodes.title: The Face of a Cultured Man
episodes.blurb: Lady Campbell's gong and white gloves, a boxing match that goes wrong for the right reasons, a scandal in the Jesmond Star, a vicar kissed by a pug, and a dream of an electric iron that smooths the whole world flat.

episodes.title: The Triumphant Sun
episodes.blurb: The Salvation Army knocks on every door, the seaside is too hot, a blue envelope arrives, and Campbell, who always believed that everything must be reasonable, finds the one thing that is not. Zamyatin's satire ends at half past nine.

glossary: Jesmond
a respectable suburb of Newcastle upon Tyne, where Zamyatin lived while supervising the building of icebreakers in 1916-17.
vicar
the priest of an Anglican parish; here the Reverend Dooley of St Enoch's.
pince-nez
spectacles without arms that clip onto the nose.
Honorary Bell-Ringers
a parish society; here a body of pious busybodies who decide what is moral.
Salvation Army
an evangelical Christian charity with brass bands and a military style.
bobby
a London policeman, from Sir Robert Peel.
Marquess of Queensberry rules
the rules of modern boxing, from 1867.
Rizzio
David Rizzio, secretary of Mary, Queen of Scots, murdered in 1566.
Waterman pen
the best-known fountain pen of the day.
the Empire
a music hall in the town.
summary: In a respectable English town, a vicar who has reduced life to timetables is thrown off his rails when a stranger is run over outside his house. Yevgeny Zamyatin's satire of English order, written in Newcastle in 1917 by the author of We, is funny, sharp and quietly terrifying.
site_description: In Jesmond, an English town where everything, from the Sunday gentlemen to the doorsteps, is made at the same factory, the Reverend Dooley has reduced life to the timetables of his Covenant of Compulsory Salvation. Then a square-chinned stranger, Campbell, who believes that whatever ought to be, is, is knocked down outside his house, and the machinery begins to fail. Zamyatin wrote it in 1917 while he was building icebreakers in Newcastle, and it is the satire of order that led to his novel We.

ru.description: Викарий Дьюли превратил жизнь в расписание. Но в воскресенье у его дома под автомобиль попадает квадратный мистер Кембл, и машина викария начинает ломаться. Сатира Замятина на английский порядок, написанная в Ньюкасле в 1917 году.
